title: Strong embedding conjecture for permutation polytopes
statement:
Let $P$ be a $d$-dimensional permutation polytope. A permutation polytope is the convex hull of permutation matrices associated with a permutation group, and two polytopes may be combinatorially equivalent or lattice equivalent.

**Strong embedding conjecture.** There exists a permutation group $G\leq S_{2d}$ such that $P(G)$ is combinatorially equivalent, or more strongly lattice equivalent, to $P$.

The bound $2d$ is suggested to be sharp by the example of the $d$-cube, while the paper notes that the existence of some bound follows from an earlier proposition. The claim is presented as open.
source_name: Barbara Baumeister, Christian Haase, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz, “On permutation polytopes”, arXiv:0709.1615 (2007).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.1615

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2007).
